correctness.rationale: The octic is squarefree exactly when its two reciprocal quartics are distinct and neither coefficient a nor b is ±2; their unordered roots in the coefficient quadratic give 36 rational pairs and 55 conjugate pairs. Independently I found all the smooth rows by gcd with the octic derivative, and identified the split locus by constructing unordered pairs of distinct rational a,b not ±2. The quotient maps have degree two, yield the stated quartics (all squarefree on the open locus), and correspond to the three order-two subgroups of the Klein four action. The first cohomology invariants of each order-two subgroup have dimension two; their pairwise intersection is the trivial-character space. The total dimension six and the three nontrivial-character dimensions force trivial dimension zero once the full quotient is seen to have genus zero: the further quotient of E0 is given by x²+x^−2 and y/x², with relation v²=u²+Mu+N−2. This gives the factorization over F11 for all extensions. Without using those quotient point-count algorithms, I counted the original curves directly over degrees 1, 2 and 3; Newton identities and the Weil functional equation recover all seven coefficients of L for every row. All 91 products and both CSV tables agree, giving 28 spectra, 8 split, 23 nonsplit, 3 shared and 20 nonsplit-only. The point and p-rank histograms also agree; exactly three of the five maximizers are nonsplit. The table labels 'Split Δ' and 'Nonsplit Δ' must be read as the prose defines them, namely by the square class of δ, not that of the full smoothness discriminant.
residual_risks: The census counts coefficient-marked models, not isomorphism classes or twists. Split/nonsplit concerns the marked reciprocal factorization only, not the Jacobian.

value.rationale: The rational descent of the displayed reciprocal factors is an intrinsic question of the marked normal form, and confining arithmetic computation to separately rational factors would miss 20 of the 28 isogeny types that actually occur. The exact spectrum distinguishes ranks from full extension-field arithmetic and is useful for comparing presentations or sampling this standard family. This is a finite family invariant, not a general algorithmic or moduli classification.
residual_risks: The split/nonsplit labels need not descend to the set of unmarked isomorphism classes.
